name: AD CS ESC3 — Enrollment Agent Certificate Abuse
description: Two-step attack: (1) obtain an enrollment agent certificate, (2) use it to enroll on behalf of any user including DA against a second vulnerable template.

steps.label: Convert EA cert to PFX
steps.command: openssl pkcs12 -in ea_cert.pem -keyfile ea_key.pem -out ea_cert.pfx -export -passout pass:<password>

steps.label: Step 2: Enroll on behalf of Administrator

examples.label: ESC3 - enroll on behalf of DA (lab template)

recommended.note: Enumerate the domain first to locate the CA and a vulnerable certificate template
ESC1 simpler if template allows SAN
DCSync after gaining DA via cert auth

notes: ESC3 = Certificate Request Agent EKU. Requires: a template with that EKU + another template allowing enrollment agent enrollment.

defense.why_it_works: ESC3 abuses the Enrollment Agent certificate type. An enrollment agent certificate (EKU: Certificate Request Agent) allows the holder to request certificates ON BEHALF OF other users. If a low-priv user can obtain an enrollment agent certificate, and there exists a template that (a) requires enrollment agent approval AND (b) allows the enrollment agent to supply any subject, the attacker uses the enrollment agent cert to issue a certificate authenticating as any user including DA.
defense.prerequisites: Domain user with access to enroll in a template with Certificate Request Agent EKU. A second template allowing enrollment agent certificate requests with a user-specifiable SAN. Certify.exe or Certipy. Rubeus for PKINIT.
defense.impact: T1649 Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates. Two-step certificate abuse: first obtain enrollment agent cert, then issue fraudulent user certificate. Same end result as ESC1 — authenticate as any domain user. Slightly more complex but often exists when ESC1 is patched but enrollment agent templates remain.
defense.detection:
Event 4887 on CA: certificate request signed by an enrollment agent (RequestedBy field shows enrollment agent account, not the subject). MDI: 'Suspected AD CS ESC3 abuse'. CA audit: certificate requests using Certificate Request Agent EKU where the requested subject differs from the enrollment agent's identity.
Abnormal AD CS certificate enrollment and usage; registry access to certificate storage; unusual processes exporting or accessing private keys (DET0240/AN0671).
File access to certificate directories; OpenSSL or PKCS#12 utilities exporting/modifying certificates; processes accessing sensitive key storage paths (AN0672).
Keychain API calls and file access to ~/Library/Keychains or /Library/Keychains for stored certificates and private keys (AN0673).
Abnormal certificate enrollment in identity platforms; unexpected use of token-signing certificates; unusual CA configuration modifications (AN0674).
defense.artifacts: CA Event 4887: certificate issued via enrollment agent | MDI: ESC3 AD CS alert | CA audit: enrollment agent template used for cross-user issuance | Event 4768: PKINIT auth using fraudulently issued cert
defense.prevention:
Restrict enrollment agent template enrollment to CA administrators only. Require CA Manager Approval on templates that allow enrollment agent-based issuance. Audit all templates with Certificate Request Agent EKU. Disable enrollment agent templates if not required for legitimate workflows (e.g., smart card enrollment stations).
Active Directory Configuration: Treat CA servers as tier-0 assets; harden abusable CA settings; disable SAN usage in authentication protocols to enforce strict user mappings; enforce CA Certificate Manager approval for templates with SAN issuance requirements.
Audit: Check and remediate unneeded certificates and common misconfigurations (enrollment permissions, overly permissive templates) via certsrv.msc, certutil.exe, PSPKIAudit, and Certify.
Disable or Remove Feature or Program: Disable old/dangerous auth protocols (NTLM) and unnecessary AD CS web/enrollment server roles.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Secure certificates and private keys; use TPM or HSM; enforce HTTPS and Extended Protection for Authentication.
defense.evasion: Two-step process — split over time to avoid correlation of the two certificate requests. Use the final certificate for PKINIT auth only (minimal log footprint post-issuance).
defense.misconfiguration: Enrollment agent certificate template accessible to Domain Users. Templates allowing enrollment agent to supply subject. No CA Manager Approval on enrollment agent issuance. CA auditing not enabled.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# ESC3 requires two vulnerable templates:
# Template 1: Enrollment Agent (Certificate Request Agent EKU) — accessible to Domain Users
# Template 2: User template — allows Enrollment Agent to enroll on behalf of others

Certify.exe find /vulnerable
# [ESC3] Enrollment Agent Certificate:
# Template: ESC3-CertRequestAgent
# Enrollment: Domain Users
# EKU: Certificate Request Agent
# [ESC3] Template allowing enrollment agent:
# Template: User
# Enrollment: Domain Users
# No enrollment agent restriction
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict enrollment agent template to CA admins only:
# Certificate Templates → ESC3-CertRequestAgent → Security
# Remove 'Domain Users' enrollment permission
# Add only 'CA Administrators' or specific smart card enrollment station accounts

# Require Manager Approval on all enrollment agent issuances:
# Template Properties → Issuance Requirements
# → 'This number of authorized signatures': 1
# → 'Application policy': Certificate Request Agent
# → CA certificate manager approval: CHECK

# Audit enrollment agent certificate usage:
# CA audit Event 4887 → filter for Certificate Request Agent EKU in certificate chain
